biography.plain_text: Italian banker Ennio Doris founded Programma Italia in 1982 after building a career in banking, insurance and financial advice. He developed it into Banca Mediolanum, combining a national adviser network with investment, insurance and online banking services. Doris remained the group's founder-chairman and a major shareholder until shortly before his death in 2021.

long_biography.plain_text:
Ennio Doris began as a bank employee before moving into retail financial advice, where he learned how to build and lead adviser networks. Programma Italia applied that experience to household savings: a nationwide network offered insurance, savings and pension advice through a single adviser relationship.

The business broadened into asset management, insurance and banking, listed publicly and became Banca Mediolanum. Doris served as chief executive and chairman over different periods, then became honorary chairman in November 2021. His wealth was tied principally to shareholdings in the listed founder-built group. Client deposits, managed savings and the bank's balance-sheet assets belonged to Banca Mediolanum, not to Doris personally.
